newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end higher, gains seen capped.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end higher, gains seen capped.

text.p: Austrian shares ended higher on Wednesday, boosted by strong international leads amid selective buying interest, but traders said the market lacked the impetus for further gains in the short term.

The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 10.54 points or 0.88 percent to close at 1,209.71 points, well below the day's high of 1,215,25 points. Among its components, 15 gainers outweighed four losers, one issue closed unchanged.
"There was interest in just a few shares," said one trader, adding that gains in top shares OMV and VA Technologie alone had accounted for a quarter of the index's overall rise.
Market participants said they expected volumes to remain thin and that prices were likely to consolidate over the next few days. "I think 1,210 points is the limit at moment," said one.
Fireproof materials maker Radex Heraklith emerged as the top gainer, up 2.67 percent or 12.50 schillings at 480 schilling on heavy turnover of 91,500 shares.
Oil and chemicals group OMV rose 29 schillings to 1377, while engineering group VA Technologie firmed 33 schillings to close at 1851.

Brick maker Wienerberger was down 11.90 at 2,245.30 schillings. Trader blamed the decline on profit taking after recent gains ahead of Tuesday's release of a limp set of 1996 earnings and a buoyant outlook for the current year.
The May ATX future ended up 10 points at 1,202.
